sources.entry: Gruyere: Web Application Exploits and Defenses

summary.title: Web Application Exploits and Defenses (Part 1)
summary.one_liner: A hands-on Google codelab that teaches web security by setting up your own sandboxed instance of the deliberately vulnerable Gruyere app and getting familiar with its features before attacking them.
keywords: capture the flag style web hacking
takeaways: Gruyere is a small, deliberately vulnerable web app; each user gets a sandboxed instance at a unique URL under google-gruyere.appspot.com.
The source code is public, so you can do white-box testing or run the app locally to debug and fix bugs.
Features such as HTML snippets, file upload, web admin, account creation, a custom template language and AJAX refresh each add attack surface.

The codelab's first part is a familiarization walkthrough; later sections cover XSS, client-state manipulation, XSRF, XSSI, path traversal, DoS, code execution, configuration and AJAX vulnerabilities.
summary.summary: This is Part 1 of Google's Gruyere codelab, written by Bruce Leban, Mugdha Bendre and Parisa Tabriz. It explains how to start a personal Gruyere instance at google-gruyere.appspot.com/start, describes the main files (gruyere.py, data.py, gtl.py, sanitize.py) and lists the features that introduce vulnerabilities. It ends with a set of familiarization tasks such as creating an account, a snippet and an upload before the attacks begin. The table of contents previews the vulnerability categories covered in later parts.
